# Building pay-off: 100 games per bot, seeds 1 to 100

Variant: {"mapId":"millValley"}. "Touching nature" (k) counts the 4 squares N, E, S, W that are nature (including river and sea).

Theory assumes each touching nature square supplies the map's average habitat at light use (B 0.8). Land: POL 1.04, GRN 1.60, WAT 1.05. Sea (for fleet and wind farm): POL 0.00, GRN 0.80, WAT 0.32. Received is capped at 6. Theory ignores waste tokens and pollution, and gives a business park its full bonus for homes. Net = income x happiness multiplier - waste bill (1 per waste token that touching nature cannot soak up). Food is shown separately: each unit saves £1 of food the town would otherwise buy, and each resident eats 1.

## Bots

| Bot | Rule | Mean H | Tile-turns | Waste bills and fertiliser as % of income | Food bought as % of income | Event damage as % of income | Tiles at risk hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| random | Picks pass, build or restore at random, then a random legal choice and square. | 2.1 | 43630 | 157% | 3% | 9% | 1682/2219 (76%) |
| greedy | Takes the build or restoration with the best gain in this turn's GDP per pound spent (but builds the best home when behind the housing target's pace); passes if nothing gains. | 4.8 | 57190 | 56% | 2% | 7% | 1735/2908 (60%) |
| nature | Builds only when short of food (a farm or fleet) or of the housing target (a home), on the square with most nature touching it; otherwise makes the restoration that would add most GDP once grown, then most happiness, then most biodiversity. | 3.9 | 57853 | 80% | 1% | 8% | 1841/3043 (60%) |
| balanced | Builds like greedy (including keeping pace with the housing target), but only off ancient habitat and where the new tile keeps at least two nature squares touching it; otherwise restores like the nature bot. | 4.5 | 67086 | 70% | 1% | 10% | 2472/3431 (72%) |
